title: Generalized Loschmidt echoes associated with operational quantum non-Markovianity
abstract: Non-Markovianity can be characterized by performing a series of successive measurements and analyzing departures of the corresponding outcome statistics from a Markovian probabilistic structure. Considering a system coupled with its environment via a dephasing interaction, we show that joint outcome probabilities can be written in terms of a set of two-time environment correlations. Their definition involves forward and backward propagators with different Hamiltonians, associated with a recently introduced generalization of standard Loschmidt echoes [Cormick and Budini, Phys. Lett. A 593, 132011 (2026)]. This result establishes a solid connection between quantum non-Markovianity defined in an operational (measurement-based) way and complex quantum dynamics studied through their sensitivity to dynamical perturbations. We find conditions that guarantee a Markovian (system) behavior and also determine how the generalized echoes can identify information exchanges between the system and its environment. We illustrate our ideas considering examples of spin environments that realize these different dynamical regimes.
summary: This paper connects the concept of Generalized Loschmidt Echoes (GLEs) to the operational definition of quantum non-Markovianity for open systems. By analyzing joint probabilities from sequential measurements, the authors show that GLEs quantify memory effects and information exchange between the system and its environment. This provides a robust diagnostic tool for understanding complex quantum dynamics beyond simple Markovian approximations.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous connection between quantum non-Markovianity, defined operationally via sequential measurements, and generalized Loschmidt echoes (GLEs). It seeks to characterize memory effects in open quantum systems using this diagnostic tool.
main_result: The set of GLEs characterizes operational quantum non-Markovianity for dephasing interactions. The fulfillment of Markovian conditions implies specific semigroup properties for the standard Loschmidt echo, linking dynamics back to environmental passivity.
method: The analysis involves calculating joint outcome probabilities $P(z, y, x)$ for three sequential measurements and comparing them against the classical Markov chain structure. This is done by deriving explicit forms for GLEs using unitary microscopic descriptions.
model_or_system: The system consists of a small quantum system (like a qubit) coupled to an environment via a dephasing interaction, described by a total Hamiltonian $H_T$. The dynamics are analyzed through sequential projective measurements at three distinct time points ($0, t, t+	au$).
key_observables: Generalized Loschmidt Echoes ($	ilde{E}_{ss}(t, 	au)$), joint outcome probabilities $P(z, y, x)$, and the difference $|	ext{E}^{++} - 	ext{E}^{--}|$ which quantifies non-commuting quantum properties.
important_parameters: Time delays ($t, 	au$), coupling strength (implied by dephasing interaction), and the specific measurement basis chosen for projection.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a unitary microscopic description of the open system dynamics and assumes a dephasing nature for the system-environment coupling.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces GLEs as generalizations of standard Loschmidt echoes. It then connects these echoes to operational non-Markovianity by analyzing joint measurement probabilities $P(z, y, x)$. Finally, it derives conditions under which the system dynamics revert to a Markovian process.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool (GLEs) rooted in quantum measurement theory to detect memory effects and information backflow in open quantum systems, bridging theoretical echo concepts with practical operational definitions of non-Markovianity.
